hero.headline: Federal judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal district judge in Washington ordered President Trump to remove his name from the Kennedy Center within two weeks. The Friday ruling also halted the planned closure of the performing arts venue, which had been scheduled to shut down later this year for renovation work.

The order requires Trump to remove his name from the building itself and from signage around the facility. The judge found that the Kennedy Center's board overstepped its legal authority by unilaterally allowing the name change.

The decision blocks Trump's effort to renovate the Kennedy Center. The facility had been preparing to close to allow construction to begin on the project.

The Kennedy Center serves as the nation's performing arts venue in the capital. The board's decision to add Trump's name to the building had preceded the planned renovation work.

The judge's order gives the president a two-week deadline to comply with the removal requirement. The ruling specifically cited the board's lack of statutory authority to make the naming decision on its own.

The closure that had been planned for later this year will not proceed as scheduled. The renovation project that was tied to the closure now faces an uncertain timeline following the court's intervention.

The order represents a legal setback for the administration's plans for the cultural institution. The Kennedy Center had been moving forward with preparations for both the name change and the associated construction work before the court stepped in.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran cease-fire proposal
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers for two hours at the White House about a possible extension but announced no agreement.
cards.body: President Trump met with advisers at the White House for two hours to discuss a potential cease-fire extension with Iran. The meeting came after the US and Iran confirmed they had agreed on a framework for a deal. Despite earlier signals that Trump was prepared to announce a decision, no final determination was made public following the discussions.

cards.headline: SpaceX wins $4.16 billion Space Force contract for missile-tracking satellites
cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX a contract to build a satellite network for tracking airborne targets as part of the Golden Dome program.
cards.body:
SpaceX received a $4.16 billion contract from the U.S. Space Force to build missile-tracking satellites for the "Golden Dome" defense system. The sensor-equipped satellites will enable the military to detect and track airborne targets from space.

The contract award is part of SpaceX's growing government portfolio. According to the company's IPO filing, SpaceX generated one-fifth of its 2025 revenue from government contracts, with the Space Force awarding the company $6.45 billion in total contracts ahead of its planned public stock offering.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in new Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The Space Force awarded SpaceX $6.45 billion in new contracts as the company prepares for a public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX has been awarded $6.45 billion in contracts from the US Space Force. The company is preparing for an initial public offering, and these government contracts come at a significant time in its corporate development.

Government work represents a substantial revenue stream for SpaceX. According to its IPO filing, government contracts accounted for one-fifth of the company's total revenue in 2025.

cards.headline: Stock markets hit fresh records as oil prices decline
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq closed at new highs, capping a strong month fueled by technology gains and hopes for a Middle East deal.
cards.body:
U.S. stock indexes reached record highs as technology stocks drove gains. The S&P 500 extended its winning streak, with Dell among the top performers in the tech sector.

Oil prices fell sharply following reports of progress toward a U.S.-Iran ceasefire agreement. Brent crude futures declined 1.3% to around $92, down 19% since the end of April. Lower energy costs combined with strength in artificial intelligence-related stocks propelled the market rally.

cards.headline: Oil prices fall on signs of potential Iran agreement
cards.teaser: Oil prices dropped as investors weighed tentative indications of progress toward a U.S.-Iran pact to extend
cards.body:
Oil prices dropped sharply on Thursday following reports of a potential breakthrough in US-Iran negotiations. A proposed extended ceasefire, pending Donald Trump's approval, triggered the decline in global oil markets.

Brent crude futures fell 1.3% on Friday to around $92 per barrel. The decline is part of a broader downward trend, with prices down 19% since the end of April as investors grew increasingly hopeful about resolving tensions in the region. Stock markets rallied on the same optimism.

cards.headline: SEC proposes repealing corporate climate disclosure rule
cards.teaser: The Securities and Exchange Commission moved to eliminate a rule requiring companies to report greenhouse gas emissions and climate risks.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission has proposed repealing a climate disclosure rule that required companies to report their greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related risks. The rule was put in place under the Biden administration.

The proposed repeal reverses the SEC's earlier effort to mandate corporate climate disclosures, which was intended to provide investors with information about how climate change could affect companies. The move reflects the current administration's direction on environmental regulations affecting businesses.

hero.headline: Russian drone strikes Romanian apartment building, injuring civilians
hero.body:
A Russian drone struck an apartment building in Romania near the Ukrainian border, injuring two people in the first civilian casualties from such an incident in the NATO member country. Romanian officials confirmed the strike and condemned Russia for the attack.

Romania is a member of NATO, and the security alliance issued a statement condemning what it described as Russian recklessness. The incident sharply escalated tensions between the alliance and Moscow.

The strike occurred near the Ukrainian border, where drones from the ongoing war have increasingly crossed into Romanian territory. Officials said this was the first such incident to cause civilian injuries in Romania, though drones have previously entered Romanian airspace.

A Russian official warned that Europe should prepare for more drone incidents following the Romania episode. The official told European countries that their peaceful sleep is over, according to reports.

NATO member states condemned Russia after the attack. The alliance's response highlighted concerns about Russian military operations affecting countries beyond Ukraine.

Romanian authorities said the drone hit the residential building, causing damage and wounding two civilians. The extent of their injuries was not specified in official statements.

The incident represents a significant development in the conflict, marking the first time Russian drones have caused casualties on NATO territory during the war in Ukraine. The strike raised questions about potential responses from NATO and individual member countries.

Drones crossing into Romania from the nearby war zone have become a growing threat, according to officials. The proximity of the conflict to NATO borders has created ongoing security concerns for alliance members in the region.

Russian officials have not apologized for the strike or indicated any change in military operations near NATO borders. The warning about future incidents suggested continued risk of similar events affecting European countries.

cards.headline: Trump delays decision on Iran cease-fire proposal
cards.teaser: The president met with advisers for two hours at the White House about a possible extension but announced no agreement.
cards.body: President Trump met with advisers at the White House for two hours to discuss a potential cease-fire extension with Iran. The meeting came after the US and Iran confirmed they had agreed on a framework for a deal. Despite earlier signals that Trump was prepared to announce a decision, no final determination was made public following the discussions.

cards.headline: Canadian man pleads guilty to aiding 14 suicides by selling toxic chemicals
cards.teaser: The man sold lethal substances online to people who used them to kill themselves, avoiding a murder trial.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law appeared in an Ontario courtroom and pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide. Prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges as part of the agreement. Law had mailed "suicide packets" containing lethal chemicals and instructions to more than 100 people across multiple countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Australia, and New Zealand.

Sentencing is scheduled for September. Families of victims in Britain have called for Law to face additional charges there, citing 79 deaths linked to his actions in the UK alone.

cards.headline: European Union to release billions withheld from Hungary after Orban defeat
cards.teaser: The EU is set to release 16 billion euros as Hungary moves to enact anti-corruption and rule of law policies.
cards.body:
The European Union will release more than 16 billion euros to Hungary that had been frozen under Viktor Orbán's leadership. The decision follows the election of new Prime Minister Péter Magyar last month, with EU Commission President Ursula von der Leyen describing it as evidence of "winds of change" in the country.

The breakthrough comes as Hungarian police announced they will permit next month's Pride parade in Budapest to proceed. This marks a reversal from the previous government's attempts to block the event last year. Magyar's administration has characterized the EU funding release as a historic breakthrough for the country.

cards.headline: Ghana parliament passes bill criminalizing LGBTQ+ identification
cards.teaser: Same-sex acts are now punishable by jail terms under legislation targeting gay, lesbian and transgender people.
cards.body:
Ghana's parliament has passed legislation that criminalizes same-sex conduct, with violators facing jail time. The bill specifically targets individuals who identify as gay, lesbian, or transgender.

The new law significantly strengthens existing restrictions on LGBTQ+ people in Ghana, establishing criminal penalties based on sexual orientation and gender identity.

cards.headline: Trump boat strikes fail to reduce cocaine flow to US, researchers say
cards.teaser: Despite a rising body count off South America, cocaine remains as easy to obtain in many US areas as before the strikes began.
cards.body:
Military strikes on boats off the South American coast have not curbed the flow of cocaine into the United States, according to experts and researchers. The operations have resulted in an increasing number of deaths but have not made the drug harder to obtain.

Cocaine is as easy to get in many parts of the United States as it was before the strikes began, researchers said. The findings suggest that the military approach has failed to disrupt drug trafficking networks despite the casualties inflicted on smugglers.

cards.headline: Iran hard-liners attempt to derail US negotiations
cards.teaser: A small but vocal faction is using rallies, state media and public statements to undermine talks.
cards.body:
A political struggle is underway in Iran as hard-liners work to undermine potential negotiations with the United States. This small but vocal faction has organized rallies and leveraged state media and public statements to oppose the talks.

The U.S. and Iran have agreed on a framework for a deal, according to officials. President Trump met with his advisers to make a final determination on the agreement, though no deal has been announced yet.

hero.headline: US military strike in Pacific kills two, death toll from boat attacks exceeds 200
hero.body:
The US military conducted another strike on a vessel in the eastern Pacific, killing three men and bringing the overall death toll from such operations above 200 people, according to an announcement by US Southern Command on Friday.

The strike marked the third attack this week as the Trump administration escalates what it describes as a campaign against "narcoterrorism." A similar operation in the Caribbean Sea on Monday killed two people. Southern Command stated that the vessel was "engaged in narco-trafficking operations" and operated by a designated terrorist organization, though it provided no identifying details or evidence.

Southern Command described those killed as "male narco-terrorists" and said intelligence confirmed the vessel was traveling along known drug trafficking routes while conducting smuggling operations. The command noted that no US military forces were harmed in the strike.

The cumulative death toll of more than 200 represents fatalities across multiple strike operations conducted by US forces in recent months. More than 190 people have been killed since September in operations labeled as targeting narcoterrorism.

However, the lack of publicly provided evidence has sparked significant debate about the legality and necessity of the strikes. The Trump administration has not released definitive proof that the targeted vessels were involved in drug trafficking, prompting scrutiny from legal experts and human rights organizations.

Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International have characterized the strikes as "unlawful extrajudicial killings." The American Civil Liberties Union has described the Trump administration's assertions against targeted individuals as "unsubstantiated, fear-mongering claims."

These concerns reflect broader questions about the legal authority and oversight of the operations. Experts and human rights advocates in the United States and internationally have raised questions about whether the strikes comply with international law and due process standards.

The aggressive posture toward suspected drug trafficking vessels continues despite other international developments, including tensions with Iran. The administration has maintained that the operations are necessary measures to combat maritime drug smuggling networks operating in international waters.

The operations target boats suspected of trafficking narcotics through the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific Ocean. Southern Command's announcements have consistently used language describing the vessels as threats while offering limited transparency about the targeting process or confirmation of drug trafficking involvement.

The rising death toll and ongoing operations have drawn increasing attention to the scope and frequency of these military actions. The strikes represent a significant escalation in enforcement efforts against maritime drug trafficking, though their justification and legality continue to face scrutiny from international observers and advocacy groups.

cards.headline: Bus crash on Virginia interstate kills five people, injures dozens
cards.teaser: A bus collided with multiple vehicles on Interstate 95 in Virginia, killing five people and injuring 34 others.
cards.body:
A bus collided with multiple vehicles on Interstate 95 southbound in Stafford County, Virginia, resulting in five fatalities and 34 injuries. The crash occurred in a work zone along the highway.

State police responded to the multi-vehicle accident. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy noted that the bus driver involved in the crash does not speak English.

cards.headline: Former Attorney General Pam Bondi tells lawmakers redaction errors occurred in Epstein files release
cards.teaser: Pam Bondi testified before lawmakers about the release of Epstein files, distancing herself from the handling of the documents.
cards.body:
Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before Congress regarding redaction errors in the release of Jeffrey Epstein-related files. During her appearance, Bondi distanced herself from responsibility for the document release, shifting focus to other officials involved in handling the materials.

The testimony occurred about a month after Bondi's predecessor was removed from office by President Donald Trump. Following her congressional appearance, Democrats indicated they may pursue further inquiries into the handling of the files.

cards.headline: Louisiana approves congressional map eliminating majority-Black district
cards.teaser: Louisiana lawmakers passed a new congressional redistricting map that removes a district where Black voters hold a majority.
cards.body:
Louisiana's Republican lawmakers approved a new congressional map that dismantles one of the state's two majority-Black districts. The redistricting followed a U.S. Supreme Court ruling that found the previous map unconstitutional.

The change is expected to give Republicans an additional House seat. Critics have characterized the redistricting as gerrymandering, as it significantly alters the state's congressional boundaries and reduces Black voter representation in the House delegation.

cards.headline: Federal judge orders Trump name removed from Kennedy Center, blocks closure
cards.teaser: A judge ruled that the president cannot add his name to the Kennedy Center and prevented a planned closure of the facility.
cards.body:
A federal judge ordered the removal of Trump's name from the Kennedy Center building. The court also blocked the president's plans to close the performing arts center for a two-year renovation project.

Trump responded to the ruling by saying he has "no interest" in the Kennedy Center following the court's decision. The judge's order ensures the Washington cultural institution will remain open to the public.

cards.headline: Homeland Security secretary considers pulling customs officers from airports in sanctuary cities
cards.teaser: DHS Secretary Mullin is weighing a plan to remove customs and border protection agents from certain airports.
cards.body:
Homeland Security Secretary Mullin is considering pulling customs officers from Newark airport and other facilities in sanctuary jurisdictions, raising concerns about potential travel disruptions. The proposal targets airports in cities that limit cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

Airlines and business groups have warned that restricting international flights could create chaos. The plan under consideration would remove CBP agents from airports including Chicago's O'Hare. Questions remain about how federal immigration enforcement would operate at major events, including World Cup games scheduled in some affected cities.

cards.headline: Federal jury convicts three protesters over ICE demonstration in Spokane
cards.teaser: A jury found three people guilty of conspiracy charges stemming from a protest at an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility.
cards.body:
A federal jury in Spokane convicted three protesters, including an Army veteran who served in Afghanistan, of felony conspiracy charges related to a June 2025 demonstration against an ICE facility. The convictions represent an escalation in the Trump administration's legal approach to protest activity, according to legal experts who view the case as an attack on First Amendment rights.

The defendants now face potential sentences of up to six years in prison and $250,000 fines. The case has drawn attention from civil rights advocates concerned about the prosecution strategies being employed against demonstrators.

hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes on launch pad in Florida
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on its launch pad at Cape Canaveral, Florida during a static fire test, dealing a significant blow to Jeff Bezos's space company and its competition with SpaceX. The explosion occurred at Launch Complex 36 on Thursday night at 9pm ET, creating a massive fireball visible from over 115 miles away in Fort Pierce.

The incident happened seconds after the start of the scheduled "hotfire" test. The explosion was powerful enough to shake homes in nearby Cape Canaveral and Cocoa Beach, with shockwaves felt across Florida's space coast. Residents in South Carolina, hundreds of miles north, reported seeing a glow in the sky from the blast. Flames continued burning at the launchpad more than two hours after the explosion.

Blue Origin described the incident as an "anomaly" and confirmed that all employees were safe with no injuries reported. Bezos acknowledged the setback in a tweet, stating it was "a very rough day" but expressing determination to rebuild and continue operations.

The explosion carries serious implications for NASA's lunar program. On Tuesday, just before the blast, NASA had announced that Blue Origin won a contract to launch the first of three planned missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use for launching lunar landers to the moon for NASA, including landers that will carry astronauts to the lunar surface.

The incident also threatens NASA's timeline for returning humans to the moon within the next two years. NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that a full evaluation of the impact on the Artemis program would be conducted following a thorough investigation. Blue Origin is currently competing with SpaceX to provide a lunar lander for the Artemis IV mission scheduled for 2028, which would mark the first crewed lunar landing since 1972.

This represents the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin. Last month, a payload from the third flight of New Glenn ended up in the wrong orbit, leading the Federal Aviation Administration to temporarily ground the rocket. Thursday's test was the first static fire test since the FAA cleared the company to return to flight.

Blue Origin has invested heavily in new facilities at Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions with NASA. The company also operates its New Shepard program, which conducts suborbital flights carrying paying customers to the edge of space.

The explosion underscores the challenges of developing heavy-lift launch capability. Isaacman noted that spaceflight is "unforgiving" and developing new rockets is "extraordinarily difficult." The incident is expected to delay Blue Origin's timeline for beginning commercial operations with the New Glenn system and potentially impact other scheduled missions.

cards.headline: Train fire at Penn Station injures five, disrupts service
cards.teaser: A maintenance train caught fire at Penn Station in New York, injuring five people and causing widespread rail disruptions during rush hour.
cards.body:
A fire on a maintenance train at Penn Station injured five people and caused widespread disruptions to Amtrak, Long Island Rail Road, and NJ Transit service. The incident occurred during evening rush hour, creating commuter chaos in the corridor between Washington, D.C., and New York City.

Amtrak suspended service through Penn Station following the fire. Service later resumed through the station. The maintenance train car fire caused delays across multiple rail systems that use the busy transit hub.

cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX a contract to build a satellite network for tracking airborne targets as part of the Golden Dome program.

cards.headline: Salmonella outbreak linked to moringa supplements reaches over 100 cases
cards.teaser: A multistate salmonella outbreak tied to moringa capsules has sickened more than 100 people, prompting a product recall.
cards.body:
A salmonella outbreak tied to moringa supplements has sickened residents across Washington state and beyond, with cases exceeding 100. The contaminated products were distributed through major online and retail platforms including Amazon, Walmart, and Target.

Health officials are advising consumers to identify and dispose of affected supplements. The FDA has issued a recall of the implicated products to prevent further illness.

cards.headline: Universal Music rejects Bill Ackman's $64 billion takeover offer
cards.teaser: Universal Music Group declined a takeover proposal from billionaire investor Bill Ackman's Pershing Square, calling the bid too low.
cards.body:
Universal Music Group rejected a $64 billion takeover proposal from Bill Ackman's investment firm Pershing Square, saying the offer fundamentally undervalued the business. Pershing Square, which holds a stake in the music company, saw its acquisition plans dealt a significant setback by the rejection.

Universal Music Group owns major record labels and music publishing operations that generate substantial revenue streams across the global music industry.

hero.headline: US proposes rule allowing federal grant cancellations at any time
hero.body:
The US government has proposed new funding rules that would allow it to cancel federal research grants at any time. The proposed changes would also make peer review optional for grant applications and introduce political staff screening of grants for forbidden topics.

The proposed rules represent a departure from current practices in federal research funding. Under existing procedures, peer review serves as a standard evaluation mechanism for grant applications, with awards typically protected from arbitrary cancellation once approved.

The new framework would give federal agencies broad discretion to terminate grants without the traditional academic review process that has guided research funding decisions. Political staff would gain authority to examine grant proposals and ongoing projects for content deemed forbidden.

The proposal affects how billions of dollars in federal research funding would be allocated and managed across universities, research institutions, and other recipients of government grants. Federal agencies fund a wide range of scientific research, from basic laboratory studies to large scale projects in medicine, physics, and other disciplines.

Research institutions and scientists have historically relied on peer review to ensure that funding decisions rest on scientific merit rather than political considerations. The peer review process involves evaluation by independent experts in the relevant field who assess the quality and potential impact of proposed research.

The proposed changes would alter this arrangement by making peer review optional rather than mandatory. This would give federal administrators more direct control over which projects receive funding and which can be terminated.

The screening process for forbidden topics would add another layer of review beyond scientific merit. Political staff would examine grant applications and active projects to identify research areas or subjects that federal officials want to exclude from funding.

The proposal has not yet been finalized or implemented. Federal rule changes typically go through a public comment period before taking effect, allowing affected parties to submit feedback on proposed regulations.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to send Ebola-exposed Americans to Kenya
cards.teaser: A Kenyan court blocked the Trump administration from transferring Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for treatment.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration's plan to send Americans exposed to Ebola to Kenya for quarantine and treatment. The ruling prevents the US government from transferring exposed individuals to a facility being built in the African nation.

The White House had confirmed it was establishing a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola during an outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rather than bringing them back to the United States. Some experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could undermine treatment efforts.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in new Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The Space Force awarded SpaceX $6.45 billion in new contracts as the company prepares for a public offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX has been awarded $6.45 billion in contracts from the US Space Force. The company is preparing for an initial public offering, and these government contracts come at a significant time in its corporate development.

Government work represents a substantial revenue stream for SpaceX. According to its IPO filing, government contracts accounted for one-fifth of the company's total revenue in 2025.

cards.headline: Law enforcement dismantles botnet controlling over 17 million devices
cards.teaser: Authorities took down a botnet that had infected more than 17 million devices worldwide.
cards.body:
Law enforcement agencies dismantled a botnet that controlled more than 17 million devices. The operation shut down one of the largest known networks of compromised computers and internet-connected devices.

The botnet was linked to a Russia-based residential proxy network. Residential proxy networks route internet traffic through infected home devices, allowing operators to mask their activities by using legitimate residential IP addresses.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ad business draws support from founders
cards.teaser: An Indian court issued a ruling on Google's advertising business that drew backing from company founders and legal analysis.
cards.body:
An Indian court ruling on Google's advertising practices has drawn support from company founders who have used it to renew their criticism of the tech giant's ad business. The decision centers on how Google handles trademarked keywords within its advertising system.

Legal experts believe the ruling could prompt platforms to reconsider their policies regarding trademarked keywords. The decision may force technology companies to change how they permit advertisers to use trademarks belonging to other businesses in their ad campaigns.

cards.headline: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm tease new N1X laptop processors
cards.teaser: Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm released coordinated messages hinting at upcoming N1X laptop processors.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are coordinating teases about Nvidia's upcoming N1X laptop processors ahead of Computex this weekend. The Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts on X both posted "A new era of PC," followed by Arm's own teaser message.

Microsoft's Surface and Windows chief Pavan Davuluri also hinted at new hardware coming for developers, sharing an image of what appears to be a curved display edge. The coordinated announcements suggest the companies are preparing to reveal details about Nvidia's Arm-based chip designed for Windows laptops.

cards.headline: Apple Music service restored after multi-country outage
cards.teaser: Apple Music experienced an outage affecting users in multiple countries before service was restored.
cards.body:
Apple Music suffered an outage that affected users across multiple countries. The streaming service experienced problems that prevented users from accessing music and using search functions.

The outage marked the third major service disruption for Apple Music in two months. Some users reported issues with search functionality and saw old albums flooding their recently added sections before Apple restored service.

hero.headline: Nationals Fire Executive After Hidden-Camera Video Shows Alleged Discrimination Comments
hero.body:
The Washington Nationals dismissed a team executive after a hidden-camera video appeared to show the official saying the organization avoided featuring a conservative player on social media, according to The New York Times.

The video allegedly captured the executive implying the team discriminated against a Catholic pitcher based on religious or political views. Multiple outlets reported the executive suggested the player was intentionally excluded from the team's social media presence due to his conservative beliefs.

The Nationals have not publicly detailed the specific comments made in the video or identified the executive by name. The team also has not confirmed which player was referenced in the alleged remarks.

The incident has drawn attention from federal authorities. Fox News reported that the baseball team faces a potential Department of Justice investigation following the allegations of religious discrimination.

The executive's dismissal comes amid heightened scrutiny of workplace discrimination practices in professional sports. Religious discrimination in employment violates federal civil rights laws, which protect workers from adverse treatment based on their faith.

The hidden-camera video's origin and the circumstances under which it was recorded have not been disclosed. The Nationals compete in Major League Baseball's National League East division and play their home games in Washington, D.C.

Neither the team nor Major League Baseball has issued a formal statement addressing the potential DOJ probe. The dismissed executive has not commented publicly on the allegations or the termination.

The timing of the executive's departure coincides with the Nationals' regular season, though the team has not indicated whether interim leadership changes have been made in the wake of the dismissal. The organization employs numerous executives across its front office, marketing, and communications departments.

cards.headline: Djokovic Loses French Open Match to Teenager Fonseca
cards.teaser: Novak Djokovic fell to 19-year-old Joao Fonseca in the third round at Roland Garros, guaranteeing a first-time men's Grand Slam champion this year.
cards.body:
Brazilian teenager João Fonseca staged a remarkable comeback to defeat Novak Djokovic in a five-set thriller at the French Open. After Djokovic claimed the first two sets, Fonseca rallied to win 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 in an epic match at Court Philippe-Chatrier that stretched over four hours.

The 19-year-old's victory ends Djokovic's pursuit of a 25th Grand Slam title and marks a breakthrough moment in Fonseca's career. With the 39-year-old's elimination, the men's draw will crown a new major champion at Roland Garros.

cards.headline: Hurricanes Eliminate Canadiens, Advance to Stanley Cup Final
cards.teaser: The Carolina Hurricanes finished off the Montreal Canadiens to return to the Stanley Cup Final, where they will face the Vegas Golden Knights.
cards.body:
The Carolina Hurricanes defeated the Montreal Canadiens in Game 5 to win the Eastern Conference finals and advance to the Stanley Cup Final. The Hurricanes will face the Vegas Golden Knights for the championship.

The Canadiens' elimination extends Canada's Stanley Cup drought to 33 years. Montreal has not won the championship since 1993, and no Canadian team has captured the trophy in more than three decades. The Hurricanes previously reached the Stanley Cup Final in 2006, when they won their only championship.

cards.headline: Pentagon Recruits Troops for White House UFC Event With Fitness Requirements
cards.teaser: Military personnel must meet weight standards to receive free tickets to a UFC fight being hosted at the White House, according to Pentagon memos.
cards.body:
The Pentagon is recruiting military service members to attend a UFC fight at the White House, according to internal memos. Troops interested in receiving free tickets must meet specific weight standards to qualify for attendance.

The White House is hosting the UFC event as part of a birthday celebration. Joe Rogan has raised safety concerns about holding the fight at the executive mansion.

cards.headline: Milwaukee Upsets Fourth-Seeded Auburn in NCAA Tournament Opener
cards.teaser: The University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee defeated fourth-seeded Auburn in the opening round of the NCAA baseball tournament.
cards.body:
Milwaukee shocked Auburn in the NCAA Tournament, defeating the fourth-seeded Tigers in their regional opener. The loss marked an early exit for Auburn, which entered the tournament as one of the higher-ranked teams in its bracket.

The upset victory made headlines in Milwaukee before the city's Brewers played the Houston Astros. Auburn had been expected to advance deep into the tournament based on its seeding and regular season performance. Milwaukee capitalized on early mistakes by the Tigers to secure the win.

cards.headline: Brewers Pitcher Abner Uribe Suspended One Game for Celebration Gesture
cards.teaser: Major League Baseball suspended Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Abner Uribe for one game after he made a gesture during a game against the St. Louis Cardinals.
cards.body:
Abner Uribe received a one-game suspension from MLB for a crotch-chopping gesture during a celebration in the Brewers' victory over the Cardinals. The pitcher has appealed the disciplinary decision.

The gesture took place on video while Milwaukee was defeating St. Louis.

cards.headline: Sacramento Makes Pitch for MLB Expansion Team
cards.teaser: Sacramento leaders presented their case for bringing a Major League Baseball expansion team to West Sacramento.
cards.body:
Sacramento is pursuing an MLB expansion franchise, joining other western markets in the competition for a new team. The city's pitch emphasized its market size and capacity to support Major League Baseball.

Local fans have expressed enthusiasm for bringing professional baseball to the region, signaling community backing for the initiative. The effort represents Sacramento's formal entry into discussions around potential MLB expansion.

hero.headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning Star Wars Editor, Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, who won an Academy Award for editing the original Star Wars film, died following a battle with metastatic cancer. She was 80.

Lucas died on Wednesday in Rancho Mirage, California. Lucasfilm posted a statement mourning her death.

She was one of three editors who shared the Oscar for Star Wars. Lucas also edited several iconic films of the 1970s, including Taxi Driver.

Marcia Lucas was formerly married to Star Wars creator George Lucas. Her editing work on the original trilogy helped shape one of the most influential film franchises in cinema history.

The Academy Award she received recognized her contribution to the 1977 film that launched the Star Wars saga. Her work involved assembling the final cut of a movie that would go on to redefine science fiction filmmaking and popular culture.

Beyond Star Wars, her editing credits on films like Taxi Driver demonstrated her range across different genres during a transformative period in American cinema. The 1970s marked a creative renaissance in Hollywood filmmaking, and Lucas played a significant role in shaping some of its most memorable works.

Lucasfilm expressed deep sadness at her passing in their official statement. The company acknowledged her contributions to the Star Wars legacy and the broader film industry.

Her death removes one of the key creative figures behind the original Star Wars film, joining other members of that production team who have passed away in recent years. The editing of Star Wars was a collaborative effort, but her role in crafting the final version of the film earned her recognition as one of the editors who made the finished product possible.

cards.headline: Music Executive Clive Davis Hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old record industry executive was admitted to a New York City hospital following a respiratory issue.
cards.body:
Clive Davis, the music industry executive, was hospitalized in New York City following a respiratory issue. He is 94 years old.

Davis has been a prominent figure in the music business for decades. His career has included discovering and working with numerous successful recording artists across multiple generations.

cards.headline: More Than Half of Freedom 250 Performers Cancel Appearances
cards.teaser: Over half of the scheduled performers for the Great American State Fair concerts have dropped out, citing politics and threats.
cards.body:
More than half of the artists scheduled to perform at the Trump-backed Great American State Fair concerts have withdrawn from the event. Artists including Martina McBride and Morris Day have canceled their appearances due to political concerns and threats.

The Freedom 250 concert series is scheduled for the National Mall in Washington on July 6 to commemorate the nation's 250th birthday. The cancellations have drawn public attention, with commentators like Bill Maher criticizing the event on his show "Real Time."

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Tour Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling the rest of his 2026 concert schedule to focus on his health.
cards.body:
The 92-year-old singer announced Friday that he is canceling his remaining concert dates for 2026 to focus on his health. Valli, known for his dedication to touring throughout his career, made the decision due to ongoing health concerns.

In a statement shared on social media, Valli apologized to fans who had purchased tickets to the canceled shows. The legendary performer expressed his regret at having to disappoint his audience.

cards.headline: A24's Backrooms Film Exceeds $10 Million in Previews
cards.teaser: The horror film directed by 20-year-old Kane Parsons has already earned more than $10 million before its nationwide theatrical release.
cards.body:
Backrooms, the latest feature from A24 and the directorial debut of Kane Parsons, has grossed more than $10 million in preview screenings. The 20-year-old filmmaker's horror movie is now playing in theaters nationwide.

The film stars Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, Mark Duplass, Finn Bennett, Avan Jogia, and Lukita Maxwell. The movie is inspired by an original YouTube series.

cards.headline: Pennsylvania Mayor Criticizes Officer Who Left for Love Island USA
cards.teaser: A Pennsylvania mayor publicly criticized a police officer who departed the force to appear on the reality television show.
cards.body:
A mayor in Pennsylvania spoke out against a police officer who left the department to participate in Love Island USA. The mayor expressed frustration with the officer's departure.

The eighth season of Love Island USA is set to feature cast members including a salon owner from Salem. The show's season 8 cast reveal is scheduled to be announced soon.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Urges Governor Candidates to Support Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman called on gubernatorial candidates to back uncapped tax incentives for film and television production.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman called on candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and television production. She made the appeal outside Radford Studios on Friday.

Raman appeared with entertainment industry figures who support her mayoral campaign, including Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon. She said the goal is to ensure Hollywood remains competitive as a production center.

hero.headline: Federal judge orders Trump's name removed from Kennedy Center
hero.body:
A federal district judge in Washington ordered President Trump to remove his name from the Kennedy Center within two weeks. The Friday ruling also halted the planned closure of the performing arts venue, which had been scheduled to shut down later this year for renovation work.

The order requires Trump to remove his name from the building itself and from signage around the facility. The judge found that the Kennedy Center's board overstepped its legal authority by unilaterally allowing the name change.

The decision blocks Trump's effort to renovate the Kennedy Center. The facility had been preparing to close to allow construction to begin on the project.

The Kennedy Center serves as the nation's performing arts venue in the capital. The board's decision to add Trump's name to the building had preceded the planned renovation work.

The judge's order gives the president a two-week deadline to comply with the removal requirement. The ruling specifically cited the board's lack of statutory authority to make the naming decision on its own.

The closure that had been planned for later this year will not proceed as scheduled. The renovation project that was tied to the closure now faces an uncertain timeline following the court's intervention.

The order represents a legal setback for the administration's plans for the cultural institution. The Kennedy Center had been moving forward with preparations for both the name change and the associated construction work before the court stepped in.

cards.headline: Judge allows reopening of Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit
cards.teaser: A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's lawsuit against the IRS after intervenors challenged a settlement agreement.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. Intervenors in the case successfully argued that a proposed settlement was problematic, leading the judge to allow further examination.

Trump and the Department of Justice had previously agreed to dismiss the suit voluntarily in exchange for establishing an "anti-weaponization" fund. The judge determined this settlement arrangement warranted additional judicial review.

cards.headline: US military kills three in strike on suspected drug boat
cards.teaser: US Southern Command killed three men in a strike on a vessel accused of carrying drugs in the eastern Pacific Ocean.
cards.body:
The US military conducted another strike Friday on a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing three men. US Southern Command said the vessel was engaged in narco-trafficking operations and was operated by a designated terrorist organization.

This marks the third attack this week as part of a months-long campaign against suspected drug boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific. The latest strike brings the overall death toll from these operations above 200 people.

cards.headline: Pentagon's $9.7 billion Dell contract raises conflict of interest questions
cards.teaser: A major Defense Department contract with Dell has prompted concerns about potential conflicts after Trump promoted the company and bought its stock.
cards.body:
The Pentagon announced a five-year, $9.7 billion agreement with Dell for Microsoft software and cloud services on Wednesday. The contract is part of an effort to consolidate the department's technology infrastructure.

The deal raised questions about potential conflicts of interest after President Trump publicly praised Dell products and purchased substantial amounts of the company's stock. The timing and scope of the contract have drawn scrutiny given the president's financial interest in the company.

cards.headline: Trump endorses lieutenant governor in South Carolina race against Mace
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina gubernatorial contest, snubbing Rep. Nancy Mace's campaign for governor.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette for South Carolina governor on Friday, backing her over Rep. Nancy Mace in the Republican primary. Trump praised Evette as an "America First Patriot" in a Truth Social post, describing her as a good friend, fighter, and winner.

The endorsement is a significant blow to Mace's campaign to move from Congress to the governor's office.

cards.headline: Democrat Talarico leads Texas Attorney General Paxton by three points in new poll
cards.teaser: State Rep. James Talarico holds a narrow advantage over Attorney General Ken Paxton in a post-runoff poll of the Texas Senate race.
cards.body:
A Texas Public Opinion Research poll released Friday shows Democratic state Rep. James Talarico ahead of Republican Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Texas Senate race. Talarico received support from 47 percent of likely general election voters, compared to Paxton's 44 percent.

The survey was conducted following the primary runoff elections and measured voter preferences among those expected to participate in the general election for the Texas Senate seat.

cards.headline: Southern Command chief meets with Cuban military officials
cards.teaser: The head of US Southern Command met with senior Cuban military leaders near Guantanamo Bay amid rising tensions between the two countries.
cards.body:
Gen. Francis L. Donovan, commander of US Southern Command, met with Cuban military officials on Friday. He joined Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legra Sotolongo and other leaders near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay, according to a Southern Command announcement.

The meeting occurred during a period of heightened tensions between the US and Cuban governments. Southern Command confirmed the talks took place with senior leadership from Cuba's military establishment.
